```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

This vignette lays out the end-to-end pipeline for chamber fluxes from any
surface (soil, water, stems, leaves, ...) as it is run in practice, and shows where each `fluxqc` function
plugs into the standard `goFlux` sequence. Chunks that require an interactive
graphics device are marked and not evaluated when the vignette is built; the
non-interactive alternatives are shown next to them. See "From raw trace to
reported flux" for a fully evaluated single closure.

```
import -> auxfile -> obs.win -> window selection -> process_fluxes()
                                                     = goFlux -> best.flux -> flag_detection -> qc_screens
                                                  -> write_outputs()
```

Ebullition (bubbles under floating chambers, from saturated soils or flooded
vegetation) is an opt-in add-on switched on with `process_fluxes(ebullition =
...)`, which hands the closures to goFlux's own `goAquaFlux()` partition
(goFlux >= 0.3.0); see `vignette("ebullition", "fluxqc")`. Users of
unsaturated surfaces never need it.

## 1. Import

For an LI-7810, subset the campaign-long `.data` file to the field days before
importing; for LGR/UGGA folders with subdirectories and occasional corrupt
files, import file by file.

```{r import}
library(goFlux)
library(fluxqc)

# LI-7810: a 160 MB file -> only the field days
licor <- import_li7810_subset(
  "data/licor/TG10-01503-2026-05-01T000000.data",
  dates = c("2026-05-22", "2026-05-23", "2026-05-24"),
  outfile = "data/licor/subset.data",
  date.format = "ymd", timezone = "UTC",
  prec = c(3.5, 0.6, 45))                    # LI-7810 datasheet, 1 s (feeds goFlux's own MDF only)

# LGR / UGGA: recursive, one file at a time, nothing written to getwd()
lgr <- import2RData_flat("data/LGR1", instrument = "UGGA",
                         pattern = "_f\\d+\\.txt$",
                         date.format = "mdy", timezone = "UTC",
                         prec = c(0.35, 0.9, 200))
```

## 2. Auxfile

One row per closure with goFlux's column names. `start.time` is instrument
time; `obs.length` is the planned closure length. If notebook times were
written on a watch that disagrees with the analyzer clock, estimate the
constant offset first (a utility, not part of the default path):

```{r aux}
aux <- data.frame(
  UniqueID   = c("T26_DBH_r1", "T26_Base_r1"),
  start.time = as.POSIXct(c("2026-05-23 10:12:10", "2026-05-23 10:50:30"), tz = "UTC"),
  obs.length = 600,
  Area  = 4254,      # cm2
  Vtot  = 7.08,      # L
  Tcham = 24.5,      # C
  Pcham = 101.3,     # kPa
  campaign = "May-2026")

fc  <- find_clock_offset(licor, aux, gas = "CO2dry_ppm", search = c(-1800, 1800), auxfile = aux)
fc$offset                 # seconds to add to notebook times; inspect fc$scores before trusting it
aux <- fc$auxfile         # start.time corrected, notebook value kept in start.time_notebook

ow <- obs.win(inputfile = licor, auxfile = aux, obs.length = 600, shoulder = 120)
```

## 3. Window selection

Three routes to the same object (a `manID` data frame with `flag`, `Etime`,
`start.time_corr`, `end.time_corr`, `obs.length_corr`):

```{r windows-interactive}
# (a) interactive, every gas visible -- needs a graphics window (not RStudio's pane)
manID <- click_peak2_stacked(ow, gases = c("CO2dry_ppm", "CH4dry_ppb", "H2O_ppm"),
                             ref.secs = 600, save.plots = "plots/windows.pdf")
manID <- click_peak2_stacked(ow, gases = "auto")     # every recognised gas column present
```

```{r windows-auto}
# (b) non-interactive: sustained CO2 rise, notebook end times as a fallback/cap
ends <- data.frame(UniqueID = aux$UniqueID,
                   end.time = as.POSIXct(c("2026-05-23 10:22:30", "2026-05-23 11:02:00"), tz = "UTC"))
manID <- auto_id_rise(ow, detect.gas = "CO2dry_ppm", gases = "auto", end.times = ends,
                      trim.secs = 30, max.secs = 600, plot.dir = "plots/auto_id")
attr(manID, "log")          # review; redo any window with (a) or (c)

# (c) explicit windows from notebooks / screenshots (a wrapper over goFlux::crop.meas())
win <- data.frame(UniqueID = "T26_Base_r1",
                  start = "2026-05-23 10:51:00", end = "2026-05-23 11:01:30")
manID_c <- windows_from_table(ow, win)
# (d) uniform crop / dead band, or an automatic one, straight from goFlux >= 0.4.0
# manID <- crop.meas(manID, deadband = 30, max.obs.length = 600)
# db <- auto.deadband(manID, "CO2dry_ppm")   # best dead band per closure by r2
manID <- rbind(manID[manID$UniqueID != "T26_Base_r1", ], manID_c)
```

## 4. Flux, detection limits and QC in one call

```{r process}
CH4 <- process_fluxes(
  manID, aux = aux, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
  precision = "mad", mdf = "wassmann", conf = 0.95,        # the defaults: record-wide MAD sigma, z = qnorm(0.975) = 1.96 (2 sigma)
  extra     = NULL,                                         # or list(precision=..., mdf=..., conf=...) / "all"
  qc        = list(c0 = list(k = 1.5), co2_tracer = list(min_slope = 0), convex = TRUE,
                   min_window = list(secs = 120), ambient_start = list(sigma = 3, secs = 10),
                   noisy = list(k = 1.5),                   # per-closure sigma vs campaign sigma (diagnostic)
                   leak = list(rate = 2e-5)),               # bench leak rate, s-1; omit to skip
  group = "campaign")                                     # group = field period (MAD sigma, C0 median)
CO2 <- process_fluxes(manID, aux = aux, gastype = "CO2dry_ppm", mdf = "two_sigma")
CH4
table(CH4$fluxes$det_class_emp); table(CH4$fluxes$qc_any)
```

The same steps by hand, if you want them one at a time:

```{r manual}
CH4_flux <- goFlux(manID, "CH4dry_ppb")
CH4_best <- best.flux(CH4_flux)
CH4_best <- flag_detection(CH4_best, traces = manID, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                           precision = "mad", mdf = "wassmann", conf = 0.95, group = "campaign")
CH4_best <- qc_screens(CH4_best, traces = manID, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb", co2 = CO2$fluxes,
                       screens = list(c0 = TRUE, co2_tracer = TRUE, convex = TRUE))
```

Optionally feed the empirical precision back into goFlux so its own `MDF`
column and `flux.plot()` annotations use it:

```{r prec-back}
sig <- precision_by_id(manID, "CH4dry_ppb")
manID$CH4_prec <- sig$sigma[match(manID$UniqueID, sig$UniqueID)]
CH4_flux <- goFlux(manID, "CH4dry_ppb")     # goFlux reads the *_prec columns
```

## 4b. The bundled closures through the pipeline (evaluated)

The Figure 4 logic of the guidelines paper, illustrated there with the
author's tree-stem examples as one labelled application: closures that look
alike in a flux table until the detection flag and the QC screens are
applied. `fluxqc_examples()` ships ten anonymized real closures across
surfaces (upland tree stems, a forest soil collar, a mangrove stem, open
water) with their real geometry and the operator-clicked windows (see
`?fluxqc_examples`). Screens are plain toggles: the nine closures with
respiring surfaces run with every screen on, and the open-water closure is
run separately with `co2_tracer = FALSE`, since water has no respiratory CO2
efflux to serve as a tracer:

```{r figure4, eval = TRUE}
library(fluxqc)
ex <- fluxqc_examples()
ex$aux[, c("UniqueID", "campaign", "season_year")]
land  <- ex$data[ex$data$UniqueID != "ebullition_floating", ]
water <- ex$data[ex$data$UniqueID == "ebullition_floating", ]
screens <- list(c0 = TRUE, co2_tracer = TRUE, convex = TRUE, min_window = list(secs = 120), noisy = TRUE)
invisible(capture.output({
  res_land  <- suppressWarnings(process_fluxes(land, aux = ex$aux, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                                               group = "campaign", qc = screens))
  res_water <- suppressWarnings(process_fluxes(water, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                                               qc = modifyList(screens, list(co2_tracer = FALSE))))
}))
out <- rbind(res_land$fluxes[, c("UniqueID", "best.flux", "sigma_emp", "MDF_emp", "det_class_emp",
                                  "qc_co2_tracer", "qc_convex", "qc_noisy", "qc_any")],
             cbind(res_water$fluxes[, c("UniqueID", "best.flux", "sigma_emp", "MDF_emp", "det_class_emp")],
                   qc_co2_tracer = NA, res_water$fluxes[, c("qc_convex", "qc_noisy", "qc_any")]))
out[match(ex$aux$UniqueID, out$UniqueID), ]
```

Reading the rows: `emission_stem_semirigid` is detected and passes;
`below_detection_stem` is a good closure whose CH4 flux is below the
detection limit (kept, flagged); `failed_closure_stem` fails the CO2 tracer
screen because the chamber never sealed, so its CH4 number is meaningless
whatever its size; `ambiguous_stem` has a marginally detected CH4 change but
no CO2 rise, which the tracer screen flags for a look (a leak-free chamber on
live tissue should accumulate CO2); `uptake_stem` and `uptake_soil` are real,
detected uptakes with healthy CO2 tracers; `high_flux_wetland_stem` and the
LI-7810 closure are large clean emissions; `ebullition_floating` is open water,
processed with the CO2-tracer screen switched off (no respiratory CO2), and
its bubbles are the add-on's business. No row was removed.

## 5. Where the outputs go

```{r outputs}
write_outputs(CH4, "results/CH4")
#> results/CH4/fluxes.csv        one row per UniqueID
#> results/CH4/settings.json     every option used (methods section)
#> results/CH4/flux_plots.pdf    one page per closure (goFlux::flux.plot via flux_pdf)
#> results/CH4/ebullition_events.csv   only when the ebullition add-on ran
```

`process_fluxes()` returns a list: `fluxes`, `events` (`NULL` unless the
ebullition add-on ran), `traces` (the concentration data actually fitted),
`gastype`, `settings`.

**goFlux columns are never modified; fluxqc adds columns; nothing is
removed.** `fluxes` starts as the exact `best.flux()` table (same names, same
values) and fluxqc appends columns with distinguishable names (`*_emp`,
`qc_*`, `flux_ebullitive`, ...), so `goFlux::flux.plot()` and any other goFlux
function run on it unchanged. `flux_pdf()` replaces `flux2pdf()` only because
the latter fails with ggplot2 >= 3.5; it writes the same plots produced by
`flux.plot()`. Every column of `fluxes`, with its origin:

| column(s) | origin | produced by | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UniqueID` | goFlux (unchanged) | auxfile / `obs.win()` | closure identifier |
| `LM.flux`, `LM.C0`, `LM.Ct`, `LM.slope`, `LM.MAE`, `LM.RMSE`, `LM.AICc`, `LM.SE`, `LM.se.rel`, `LM.r2`, `LM.p.val` | goFlux (unchanged) | `goFlux::goFlux()` | linear model fit |
| `HM.flux`, `HM.C0`, `HM.Ci`, `HM.slope`, `HM.MAE`, `HM.RMSE`, `HM.AICc`, `HM.SE`, `HM.se.rel`, `HM.r2`, `HM.k` | goFlux (unchanged) | `goFlux::goFlux()` | Hutchinson-Mosier fit |
| `C0`, `Ct`, `MDF`, `prec`, `flux.term`, `nb.obs`, `k.max`, `k.mult`, `g.fact` | goFlux (unchanged) | `goFlux::goFlux()` | start/end concentration, goFlux's MDF (datasheet `prec`), (V/A)(P/RT), n, kappa bounds, g-factor |
| `best.flux`, `model`, `quality.check`, `HM.diagnose`, `LM.diagnose`, `HM.score`, `LM.score`, `*.lim`, `warn.nb.obs` | goFlux (unchanged) | `goFlux::best.flux()` | selected flux and why |
| `<group>` | fluxqc (added) | auxfile via `process_fluxes()` | grouping column merged for the screens |
| `sigma_emp` | fluxqc (added) | `flag_detection()` | per-closure precision by the chosen estimator |
| `MDF_emp`, `below_MDF_emp`, `MDF_emp_method` | fluxqc (added) | `flag_detection()` | the reported MDF, its flag, and `"<mdf> | <precision> | <conf>"` |
| `detected_emp`, `det_class_emp` | fluxqc (added) | `flag_detection()` | `emission` / `uptake` / `below detection` by `MDF_emp` |
| `sigma_<precision>`, `MDF_<mdf>_<precision>[_<conf>]` | fluxqc (added, only with `extra`) | `flag_detection()` | comparison columns |
| `qc_c0`, `qc_c0_ratio` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | C0 > k x group median |
| `qc_co2_tracer`, `qc_co2_slope` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | CO2 tracer screen (toggle it off for surfaces without respiratory CO2) |
| `qc_convex` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | accelerating trace |
| `qc_min_window` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | window shorter than `secs` |
| `qc_ambient_start`, `qc_ambient_dev_sigma` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | start already enriched vs pre-closure ambient |
| `qc_noisy`, `qc_noisy_sigma`, `qc_noisy_ratio` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | closure sigma > k x campaign sigma (disturbed closure?) |
| `qc_leak`, `qc_leak_apparent_flux` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | leak-equivalent flux >= `MDF_emp` |
| `qc_any`, `qc_note` | fluxqc (added) | `qc_screens()` | any screen fired; which |
| `ebullition_handling`, `n_ebullition_events`, `ebullition_flag` | fluxqc add-on (added only with `ebullition = "flag"`/`"split"`) | `detect_ebullition()` over `goFlux::goAquaFlux()` | bubble events per closure |
| `flux_diffusive`, `SE_diffusive`, `n_obs_diffusive`, `flux_ebullitive`, `SE_ebullitive`, `flux_total`, `SE_total`, `first_bubble_time`, `ebullition_method` | goFlux `goAquaFlux()` via the add-on (added only with `"split"`) | `goFlux::goAquaFlux()` | goFlux's partition: diffusive term on the pre-bubble window, summed bubble steps, total; `best.flux` itself stays the whole-trace fit |

`events` (add-on only): goFlux's bubble table (`UniqueID`, `start`, `end`,
`magnitude`, `SE`, `slope`, `n_used`, `overshoot`, `tau`, ...). `settings`: `fluxqc_version`, `goFlux_version`,
`gastype`, `precision`, `mdf`, `conf`, `extra`, `sigma_global`, `qc`
(parameters of each screen), `group`, `surface`, `ebullition*`, `goFlux_args`,
`best.flux_args`, `n_closures`, `date`.

## 6. Plots by hand

```{r plots}
CH4_plots <- flux.plot(CH4$fluxes, CH4$traces, "CH4dry_ppb", shoulder = 20,
                       plot.display = c("MDF", "prec", "nb.obs", "flux.term"))
CO2_plots <- flux.plot(CO2$fluxes, CO2$traces, "CO2dry_ppm", shoulder = 20)
flux_pdf(c(CO2_plots, CH4_plots), "plots/flux_results.pdf")   # ggplot2 >= 3.5 safe
```
